title: A Rivergate for the Wreck
premise: Petra Brightwater, captain of the battered sternwheeler Wreck's Fortune, is hired by a desperate government clerk to retrace the route of a vanished survey expedition up the Rivergate. He finds one survivor — the surveyor's daughter, Isla Vane — guarding her father's sealed instruments and a map of something the government will burn towns to keep quiet. As soldiers close in from downstream and the river itself turns hostile with early floods, Petra must choose between delivering the evidence to a free press in Terrapin Landing or surrendering it to save his found crew. In the end he runs the flooded gorge at night, loses his boat to the river that raised him, and gains something rarer: a family bound not by blood but by what they refused to give up.
about_author: A. M. Fairweather is the pen name of a former river pilot who spent eleven years working the inland waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels steeped in the rhythms of water, weather, and the people who make their living between them.

chapters.title: The Debt on the Dock
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Broke and one payment from losing the Wreck's Fortune, Petra accepts a suspiciously generous contract from a trembling government clerk: find the lost survey team upriver. Emotional beat: reluctant hope — the money smells wrong, but so does going under.

chapters.title: Gear With No Ghosts
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the last known campsite, Petra finds tents pitched, kettles cold, and no bodies, no tracks, no struggle — only a compass bearing scratched into a crate. Emotional beat: creeping dread; the river has swallowed men before, but never this cleanly.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Bluffs
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. Petra discovers Isla Vane hiding in the bluffs, half-starved, guarding her father's sealed instrument case. She trusts no one, least of all a man paid by the office she believes killed the survey team. Emotional beat: wary alliance forged over a shared fire.

chapters.title: What the Instruments Saw
chapters.summary: Isla's POV, with Petra listening. Against her better judgment, Isla opens the case: readings proving the government has been secretly damming and diverting the Rivergate, dooming three river towns. Emotional beat: the weight of knowledge — some cargo sinks ships.

chapters.title: Smoke Downstream
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A gunboat appears below them; the clerk's contract was bait to find Isla. Petra fakes a breakdown, hides the Wreck's Fortune in a side slough he alone knows. Emotional beat: the first open choice — he could hand her over and be rich.

chapters.title: Crew of the Willing
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Petra gathers his ragged family: engineer Old Sable, cook Marisol, deckhand twins Pip and Fen. Each chooses to stay knowing what it costs. Emotional beat: warmth against danger; the boat becomes a home worth defending.

chapters.title: The Flood Comes Early
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The secret diversions have destabilized the river; an unseasonal flood surges down the gorge, stranding them above the only rapids passage. Emotional beat: nature as the third antagonist — indifferent, enormous, honest.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Bargain
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. The clerk catches up under a flag of truce, offering amnesty for everyone if Isla surrenders the instruments. Petra stays silent, letting her decide. Emotional beat: love against duty made explicit — she realizes staying means risking them all.

chapters.title: Running the Gorge
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Night, flood-stage water, and every sandbar moved: Petra pilots the Wreck's Fortune through the gorge past the gunboat, wrecking her on the shoals below but getting his people and the evidence through. Emotional beat: triumphant grief — the river takes its toll.

chapters.title: A Rivergate for the Wreck
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. In Terrapin Landing, the story breaks; the towns are saved, the clerk exposed. Petra stands on the shore watching his boat's bones settle into the shallows — and finds he doesn't mourn. Emotional beat: resolution; survival's price paid, and a new family standing beside him on the bank.
